subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 19, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 19, 2026

Development Updates: The team landed a batch of website and infrastructure work today, keeping the public-facing properties tidy and consistent. A sync pass aligned the per-page meta Content-Security-Policy headers with the canonical policy defined in the _headers file. That was followed by removing the hard-coded Ahrefs analytics script from all pages, since it is now served through Google Tag Manager.

On the application side, AcreetionOS-Xlibre received an update to the latest Electron build for new users. This keeps the packaged experience current with upstream improvements while the team continues validating it against the XLibre stack. Expect further polish as feedback rolls in from early testers.

Infrastructure work continued across the project's hosted services with temporary mirror bootstrap commits in app_aosmium, acreetionos.gitlab.io, and the acreetionos-archive-uploader repository. These bootstrap steps lay the groundwork for smoother mirroring and archive handling. The acreetionos-blog repository also shipped a deploy update that sets the SITE variable correctly for GitHub Pages.

Community News: A significant security disclosure made the rounds today as Xint reported the NGINX2Root set of remote code execution vulnerabilities affecting nginx. If you run nginx in front of any of your services, please review the advisory and check your package versions. Patching early is far easier than explaining a compromise later.

The wider ecosystem also saw its usual midweek cadence of security updates, with AlmaLinux issuing fixes covering areas such as .NET runtimes, bind, buildah, cockpit, container networking plugins, gcc, firefox, and freerdp. AcreetionOS tracks upstream Arch packages closely, so affected components will move through our mirrors as they are validated. Always run your system updates on a maintained schedule rather than letting them pile up.

Also notable this week, Drew DeVault announced that Redict is being deprecated in favor of Valkey. For anyone running Redis-compatible caching or data services, this is a good moment to evaluate your long-term dependency plan. Valkey continues to gain traction, and monitoring the migration path now will save headaches later.

Tips & Highlights: If you maintain any of your own web properties, today's Content-Security-Policy sync is a nice reminder to audit your headers periodically. Divergent per-page policies tend to drift from the canonical source and quietly weaken your posture. A quick diff against your authoritative configuration catches that before attackers do.

For those experimenting with AcreetionOS-Xlibre, the fresh Electron update is a good reason to retest any custom tooling or packaging scripts you rely on. Small upstream changes sometimes surface in surprising ways, and early reports help the team move faster. Share what you find in the community channels so others benefit.

Finally, take a moment this week to inventory the services you depend on and note which ones are approaching end of life or deprecation, much like the Redict situation. A short written plan beats a rushed migration every time. Thanks for reading, and we will see you in tomorrow's update.
